speaker: Doctor
text: I notice your skin and eyes have a yellowish tint, which suggests jaundice. To help me determine the cause, can you tell me if you have experienced any abdominal pain, nausea, or changes in your urine or stool color recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of high-risk sexual behavior, have you experienced any fever, fatigue, or dark urine recently? I need to rule out acute viral hepatitis, so I will order specific blood work. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis Panel, Liver Function Tests, CBC

speaker: Doctor
text: Your lab results show severe liver dysfunction with significantly elevated bilirubin and enzymes, along with impaired clotting. To help pinpoint the cause, have you had any recent fever, joint pain, or noticed a rash, and do you recall any unprotected sexual encounters in the last 6 months? REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis A, B, and C Serologies, Acetaminophen Level

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal viral serologies and acetaminophen levels, we must look at other causes of acute liver failure. Do you recall consuming any wild mushrooms, or have you taken any herbal supplements or over-the-counter medications in the last week?

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ecstasy use and the exclusion of common viral and toxic causes, I need to assess for potential rhabdomyolysis or drug-induced liver injury. Have you experienced severe muscle pain, weakness, or dark, tea-colored urine following your last drug use? REQUEST TEST: Creatine Kinase, Urinalysis, Coagulation Profile

speaker: Doctor
text: With rhabdomyolysis and common viral hepatitis ruled out, I need to investigate other causes of acute liver injury. Have you consumed any energy drinks, herbal supplements, or unknown substances mixed with your drugs, and do you have a history of autoimmune conditions? REQUEST TEST: Autoimmune Liver Panel, Toxicology Screen

speaker: Doctor
text: With viral, toxic, and autoimmune causes largely excluded, I am considering metabolic or genetic etiologies like Wilson's disease. Do you have a history of neurological symptoms such as tremors or difficulty speaking, and has any family member been diagnosed with liver or neurological disorders? REQUEST TEST: Ceruloplasmin, Urinary Copper, Slit-Lamp Exam

speaker: Doctor
text: Since common viral, toxic, and metabolic causes are ruled out, I must consider acute liver failure secondary to severe rhabdomyolysis or a rare toxin, despite normal CK. Has the patient experienced seizures or prolonged muscle contractions, and is there any evidence of ingestion of unknown herbal remedies or contaminated supplements? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound, Serum Ammonia, Lactate Dehydrogenase

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal Ultrasound: Normal liver morphology, no evidence of biliary obstruction or mass lesions. Serum Ammonia: Elevated (indicative of hepatic encephalopathy). Lactate Dehydrogenase: Normal.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal imaging and serologies, combined with your history of ecstasy use and acute liver failure, strongly suggest Acute Liver Failure secondary to 1,1,3-Trimethyl-1-benzyltetrahydropyrazine (1-BZP) or similar stimulant toxicity. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Liver Failure due to Illicit Drug Toxicity (likely 1-BZP)
